text:
RECOMMENDATION: DON'T RAISE IT
LIKELIHOOD: 5

Both you and the successful candidate are women, so sex can't plausibly explain why she was preferred over you. An all-woman panel is also unremarkable — in many fields it's just who was available. Raising it would signal that you're looking for a grievance rather than examining the decision, and would undermine your credible complaints.

Those complaints are real: a panel that weighted "industry experience" over a completed PhD, six papers and four years of teaching may have deviated from the advertised criteria — and two weeks' silence on a written explanation likely breaches public-sector transparency duties.

Send a dated follow-up citing your right to reasons, then consider the university's appeals process. Age is a more plausible angle than sex, if any.
